text.p: Shares listed by media group Televisa moderated their earlier slide at mid-afternoon trade on Thursday amid changing market reaction to the sudden news that former chairman Emilio Azcarraga Milmo had died.
Televisa CPO shares were off 30 centavos to 103.70 pesos, while the group's ADRs were down 1/8 to 26-3/8.
"The news obviously hit the stock earlier on, but the ADR is off its lows," a desk trader said.
Azcarraga Milmo, known as "the Tiger", had retired for health reasons on March 4 after a quarter century of leading Televisa.
Televisa CPO shares had opened at 102.50 pesos, while their ADRs reached a low of 26-1/8 in early trade.
Traders said the news of Azcarraga Milmo's death had led initially to renewed doubts about a new management line-up announced on March 4.
The new team is led by Azcarraga Milmo's 29-year old heir, Emilio Azcarraga Jean.

"We had thought his (Azcarraga Jean's) father would be behind him, so the death came as a shock at first, but the market had already had time to get used to the new team running things," the trader added.
